sections.h2: Which Nevada laws cover a rented house?
sections.html:
NRS chapter 118A is the Nevada landlord and tenant statute for dwellings, and chapter 40 sets the court procedures for removing a tenant. A house or apartment rented as a home falls under 118A. Mobile home parks sit in a separate chapter, 118B, which this page does not cover.

Nevada's two chapters divide the work. Chapter 118A covers the rental agreement, deposits, rent increases, repairs and what each side owes. Chapter 40 covers notices to surrender and the summary eviction process after a tenant defaults or a tenancy ends.

A rental agreement cannot waive a tenant's rights under the chapter. NRS 118A.220 lists prohibited provisions, which include a tenant agreeing to give up rights or remedies, authorizing someone to confess judgment, or agreeing to pay the landlord's attorney's fees, other than a clause awarding reasonable fees to the prevailing party. Any lease terms that conflict with those rules may not hold up.

sections.h2: What happens to a tenant's lease when the owner sells?
sections.html:
The lease continues. NRS 118A.349 says that when the property is voluntarily sold, and unless the new owner and the tenant agree to change or end the lease, the new owner takes on the previous owner's rights and obligations under the rental agreement, and the tenant keeps the tenant's rights and obligations.

The new owner has to send the tenant a notice within 30 days after the sale. It must give the new owner's contact information for rent, say that the existing agreement continues through the tenancy, state the amount held as a security deposit, and warn that failing to pay rent to the new owner or follow the lease is a breach.

A seller with a tenant should plan for these points:

  • The buyer inherits a lease that may have months left, so rent, term and any renewal clauses belong in the sale paperwork.
  • The deposit must follow the property, which is covered in the next section.
  • Showing the house requires proper notice to the tenant.
  • If the buyer wants the house empty, an agreement with the tenant is the clean path. The statute leaves room for the new owner and tenant to modify or end the lease by agreement.

sections.h2: What must the seller do with the security deposit?
sections.html:
Before recording the deed, the landlord must either hand the remaining deposit to the buyer in writing or tell the buyer in writing that the deposit has been returned to the tenant. NRS 118A.244 sets that rule, and it says the successor must accept the deposit and may not demand an additional one during the term of the rental agreement.

When the landlord's interest ends by sale, the landlord must within a reasonable time do one of two things. The first is to notify the tenant in writing of the successor's name, address and telephone number and that the deposit balance was transferred. The second is to return the remaining deposit to the tenant. Either step relieves the landlord of further liability for the deposit.

Deposits carry real exposure for an owner who skips this. A landlord who fails to return the remainder within 30 days after a tenancy ends is liable for damages in an amount equal to the entire deposit, plus a further sum the court fixes of up to the amount of the deposit under NRS 118A.242.

sections.h2: Which numbers does a Nevada landlord have to know?
sections.html:
Several limits come straight from the statute, and they matter in a sale because a buyer's lawyer will check each one. This table collects the main ones from chapter 118A.

TopicRuleStatute
Security deposit cap3 months' periodic rent, including last month's rentNRS 118A.242
Return of depositItemized accounting and remainder within 30 days after the tenancy endsNRS 118A.242
Rent increase notice60 days written notice (30 days for periodic tenancies under 1 month)NRS 118A.300
Late feeNot before 3 calendar days after the due date, and no more than 5 percent of periodic rentNRS 118A.210
Landlord entryAt least 24 hours notice, at reasonable times, except in an emergencyNRS 118A.330
Cure period for habitability or lease breach by landlord14 days after written noticeNRS 118A.350, 118A.355
Essential services failure48 hours after written notice, excluding weekends and holidaysNRS 118A.380
Unlawful lockout or utility shutoffActual damages or up to $2,500 fixed by the court, or bothNRS 118A.390

NRS 118A.200 also requires a written agreement to be signed by both sides and a copy delivered free at signing.

sections.h2: Can an owner show the house to buyers while a tenant lives there?
sections.html:
Yes, with notice. NRS 118A.330 says a tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent for the landlord to enter to exhibit the unit to prospective or actual purchasers, among other purposes. The landlord must give at least 24 hours' notice of the intent to enter and may enter only at reasonable times during normal business hours, unless the tenant agrees to shorter notice or to entry outside business hours.

Emergencies are the exception, and a landlord may not abuse the right of access or use it to harass the tenant. Written notices to a tenant are served in the manner NRS 40.280 provides, according to NRS 118A.190.

A tenant who blocks lawful access can face consequences under NRS 118A.500, and a landlord who abuses access can too. Practical advice is to put the showing schedule in writing and keep it modest. A tenant who is cooperative tends to make the sale smoother, but that is common sense rather than a rule in the statute.

sections.h2: How can a landlord end a tenancy before selling?
sections.html:
Only through the notice and court steps the statutes set out, and the notice depends on the type of tenancy and the reason. NRS 40.251 says a tenant in a dwelling under chapter 118A is guilty of unlawful detainer after the lease term ends or is terminated and a notice period expires, which is at least 7 days for week-to-week tenancies and at least 30 days for other periodic tenancies. A 5 day notice applies where the tenant failed to perform basic or contractual obligations under chapter 118A.

For unpaid rent, NRS 40.253 provides a written notice requiring payment or surrender by the close of business on the seventh judicial day after service. A separate shorter path covers weekly rent tenancies of 45 days or less. Under NRS 40.2516, a tenant who fails to perform another lease condition after written notice has 5 days to comply or leave.

Notices must be served by the methods in NRS 40.280, which include delivery by the sheriff, a constable, a licensed process server or an attorney's agent. A fixed-term lease does not simply end because the owner lists the house, and NRS 118A.349 confirms the lease follows the property.

sections.h2: What is a landlord not allowed to do?
sections.html:
A landlord may not take back possession by self-help. NRS 118A.480 says possession may be recovered only through an action for possession or similar proceeding, when the tenant surrenders, or when the tenant abandons the unit. NRS 118A.390 adds that unlawfully removing a tenant, blocking entry or willfully cutting essential services gives the tenant a right to recover possession, actual damages, or an amount of up to $2,500 fixed by the court.

The tenant can file a verified complaint for expedited relief, which the statute says must be filed within 5 judicial days after the unlawful act. A landlord who skips the court process in order to deliver a vacant house to a buyer takes that risk.

Property left behind is handled by NRS 118A.460. The landlord must reasonably provide safe storage for 30 days after abandonment or eviction, and may charge reasonable costs of inventory, moving and storage. After that period, the landlord may dispose of the property if there were reasonable efforts to find the tenant, written notice of intent to dispose, and 14 days have passed since the notice. NRS 118A.520 abolishes distraint for rent.

sections.h2: What can a tenant demand when the house needs repairs?
sections.html:
A dwelling must be habitable at all times, and NRS 118A.290 defines habitability by reference to housing and health codes and to basics such as weatherproof roof and walls, working plumbing, water supply, heating and electrical systems. A landlord also may not charge fees for repairs or maintenance that are the landlord's own duty.

The tenant's remedies are staged. After written notice, the landlord has 14 days to fix a remediable failure or make best efforts. If the landlord does not, the tenant may end the lease, recover actual damages, ask the court for relief, or under NRS 118A.355 withhold rent without late fees until the problem is remedied or a good faith attempt is made. For small repairs where the cost is less than $100 or one month's rent, whichever is greater, NRS 118A.360 lets a tenant who has notified the landlord make the repair and deduct the reasonable cost from rent, up to that amount.

A tenant cannot use these remedies for conditions the tenant or a guest caused. For an owner planning to sell, unresolved repair complaints are a liability the buyer will see in the inspection, so keep written records of requests and fixes.

sections.h2: What if the seller stays in the house after closing?
sections.html:
A person who sold the property and keeps living there can be removed after a 3-day written notice to surrender, once title under the sale has been perfected. NRS 40.255 lists sale by the person, or by someone the person claims under, among the cases where holdover can be removed through the court procedures in NRS 40.290 to 40.420.

That matters to sellers who want a short rent-back after a cash sale. Put the rent-back in a written agreement with a clear end date, rent amount and deposit, because the statute treats the occupant as a holdover if the arrangement ends and the person stays.

Landlords must also tell a prospective tenant in writing if the property is the subject of foreclosure proceedings, under NRS 118A.275. A willful violation is a deceptive trade practice.

faqs.q: Does a Nevada tenant have to move when the owner sells the house?
faqs.a: No. NRS 118A.349 says the lease continues with the new owner unless the new owner and the tenant agree to change or end it. The new owner must send the tenant a notice within 30 days after the sale.

faqs.q: How much can a Nevada landlord charge for a security deposit?
faqs.a: The total of a security deposit and surety bond, including last month's rent, cannot exceed 3 months' periodic rent under NRS 118A.242. The landlord must return the remainder with an itemized accounting within 30 days after the tenancy ends.

faqs.q: How much notice must a Nevada landlord give before raising rent?
faqs.a: Written notice 60 days before the first rental payment to be increased, or 30 days for a periodic tenancy of less than one month, under NRS 118A.300.

faqs.q: How long does an eviction notice take for unpaid rent in Nevada?
faqs.a: NRS 40.253 provides a written notice to pay or surrender by the close of business on the seventh judicial day after service. A shorter period applies to certain weekly tenancies of no more than 45 days. The case then goes through the court.

faqs.q: Can a landlord change the locks or shut off utilities to clear a house for sale?
faqs.a: No. NRS 118A.480 requires a court process or a surrender or abandonment, and NRS 118A.390 lets a tenant recover possession, actual damages, or up to $2,500 as fixed by the court if the landlord locks out the tenant or interrupts essential services.

faqs.q: Who gets the security deposit when a rental is sold?
faqs.a: The seller must transfer the remaining deposit to the buyer in writing before recording the deed, or tell the buyer in writing that it was returned to the tenant, under NRS 118A.244. The buyer must accept the deposit and cannot demand an additional one during the lease term.
